_comment: Workbook exercise zone-reheat-overcooling (docs/workbook/zone-reheat-overcooling.md): the lbnl-fpu template's South-zone boxes (PFPU__<run>, the box every fault is imposed on -- see mappings/lbnl_fpu.json) with the reheat and overcooling rules of PNNL chapter 7 added. airflow_tracking and unmet_setpoint_hours are the dataset template's (the controller's active airflow setpoint VAV_PM_CFM_S_SP is trended, so a stuck damper shows as airflow off its setpoint). reheat_penalty reads the controller's reheat demand (RH_VLV_DM_S) against the AHU supply air entering the box (SA_TEMP, mapped as mixed_air_temp); overcooling_min_flow reads the zone against its cooling setpoint while the box sits at its airflow setpoint with the damper at or below 30%. Defaults throughout (weekday 07-18 occupancy, the rules' own thresholds): the point is to compare each faulted run with the fault-free one, not to tune. reheat_minimization_g36 is left out for the template's reason (the trended setpoint is the active one, not the design maximum, and G36 dual-maximum logic is for single-duct boxes); reheat_capacity_shortfall is the zone-reheat-saturated exercise's. Hourly resample: a year of 15-minute data. 0.98 (#85): RH_VLV_S, the valve's measured position, is mapped as heat_valve_position, and reheat_penalty and overcooling_min_flow read it in place of the demand, so a valve stuck shut is 0% open (the finding carries a demand-vs-position caveat instead); reheat_penalty sets fan_heat_f to 'auto', because the box fan lifts the discharge a few F above SA_TEMP with the valve shut.

basis.fan_heat_f: CAMBER judgment (0.98, #85): a fan-powered box's own fan (and, in a parallel box, the plenum air it mixes in) lifts the discharge above the entering primary air with the valve shut; 'auto' estimates that lift per box from its closed-valve samples (clipped to 0-8 F) and raises the valve-vs-discharge bounds by it
